title: CEDAR: Computing-in-pixel Edge-aware Detection and Reconstruction Architecture for High-resolution 3D Imaging
problem: SPAD-based dToF sensors for autonomous driving face power and data constraints from high-power in-pixel TDCs and multiframe histogram sampling, limiting pixel format and resolution scaling.
motivation: SPAD-based dToF sensors are essential for L5 autonomous driving but current designs are constrained by power dissipation and data bandwidth, preventing high-resolution 3D imaging implementations.
method: The sensor uses charge-domain convolution (detecting edges by measuring electrical charge patterns) to identify depth-changing regions on the chip, then applies in-memory denoising to remove noise from those pixels. By doing edge detection directly on the sensor, the system activates the time-to-digital converters (the power-hungry circuits that measure how long light takes to return) only in edge regions, slashing power consumption and data volume. A U-Net neural network then fills in the missing depth values across the entire image, reconstructing the full-resolution picture from just the sparse edge pixel data.
key_novelty: This is the first SPAD-based dToF sensor combining in-pixel edge detection with sparse reconstruction, achieving 512×512 resolution using only 3.5% sparse edge pixels and improving pixel format by 16×.
contributions: 512×512 high-resolution SPAD-based dToF sensor with 83.3 mW power consumption and 0.9 cm accuracy
In-pixel edge detection using charge-domain convolution and in-memory denoising architecture
U-Net based depth reconstruction from sparse edge pixels achieving 35.2 dB PSNR
16× pixel format and resolution improvement within same power dissipation constraints

metrics.accuracy: 0.9 cm distance, 35.2 dB PSNR, 60 fps frame rate
